# Commands Reference (auto-generated — v1.1.0)

> Generated by `scripts/gen-docs.mjs` from the live command schemas. Do not edit by hand.
> Run `npm run build && npm run docs:build` after changing a command; `npm run docs:check` (part of `npm run verify`) fails on drift.

Every command supports `--json` (compact envelope, default for agents) and `--pretty-json`. Success goes to **stdout**, errors to **stderr** with a categorized exit code. See [agent-integration.md](agent-integration.md) for the envelope contract.

## Global options

```
-V, --version        output the version number
--json               emit the unified JSON envelope (compact; default for agents)
--pretty-json        emit the same envelope with 2-space indentation
-h, --help           display help for a command
```

## Command index

| Command | Scope | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |

## `abap init`

Initialize the workspace — bind a profile, write .abap.json, inspect, clear fields, or scaffold AI agent context.

```bash
abap init [options]
```

### Options

| Option | Required | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--profile` `<name>` | no |  |  | Use an existing global profile (created with `abap profile add`). |
| `--url` `<url>` | no |  |  | SAP system URL (TTY wizard only). |
| `--client` `<client>` | no |  |  | SAP client number. |
| `--username` `<user>` | no |  |  | SAP username. |
| `--password` `<password>` | no |  |  | SAP password (stored in keychain). |
| `--language` `<language>` | no |  |  | SAP language. |
| `--insecure` | no |  |  | Skip SSL certificate verification (development only). |
| `--ca` `<path>` | no |  |  | PEM CA certificate to import into ~/.abap-cli/certificates/ and bind to this profile. |
| `--tr` `<transport>` | no |  |  | Default transport number (written to .abap.json). |
| `--package` `<package>` | no |  |  | Default SAP package (written to .abap.json). |
| `--source-dir` `<path>` | no |  |  | Base directory for `push --all` / `check --all` (written to .abap.json). |
| `--show-config` | no |  |  | Print the current workspace config (.abap.json) as JSON and exit. |
| `--unset-package` | no |  |  | Remove the `package` key from .abap.json. |
| `--unset-tr` | no |  |  | Remove the `transport` key from .abap.json. |
| `--unset-source-dir` | no |  |  | Remove the `sourceDir` key from .abap.json. |
| `--test-connection` | no |  |  | Probe TLS + auth and report results (implies --test-tls --test-auth). |
| `--test-tls` | no |  |  | Probe the TLS handshake. |
| `--test-auth` | no |  |  | Probe authentication (after TLS). |
| `--agent` `<target>` | no |  | generic, copilot, claude, cursor | Scaffold agent context files. One of: copilot \| claude \| cursor \| generic. |
| `--force` | no |  |  | Overwrite existing files when scaffolding --agent (default: skip). |
| `--yes` | no |  |  | Skip all prompts; fail if required input is missing. |
| `--non-interactive` | no |  |  | Alias of --yes. |

### Examples

- First-time bind

  ```bash
  abap init --profile DEV --tr DEVK900001 --package Z_MY_PACKAGE --yes
  ```
- Inspect current config

  ```bash
  abap init --show-config
  ```
- Scaffold agent context

  ```bash
  abap init --agent copilot
  ```

## `abap pull`

Download ABAP objects from SAP to local files.

```bash
abap pull [options] [object-name]
```

### Arguments

| Argument | Required | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `object-name` | no |  | Object name (e.g. ZCL_MY_CLASS). |

### Options

| Option | Required | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--type` `<type>` | no |  |  | Object type (CLAS, PROG, INTF, etc.). |
| `--package` `<package>` | no |  |  | Download all objects in a package (bounded by --limit). |
| `--limit` `<n>` | no | `20` |  | Batch page size for --package. |
| `--page` `<n>` | no | `1` |  | Batch page number for --package (1-based). |
| `--dir` `<path>` | no | `"src/"` |  | Output directory. |
| `--overwrite` | no |  |  | Replace local file with different content. |
| `--skip-existing` | no |  |  | Skip files that already exist. |
| `--include-tests` | no |  |  | Include testclasses source part. |
| `--include-all-parts` | no |  |  | Include every source-code part. |
| `--textpool` | no |  |  | Also pull textpool files (.texts/.selections/.headings.<lang>.properties). |
| `--active` | no |  |  | Pull the active (activated) version — the source `abap run` executes. Default: the working-area/latest version. |
| `--remote` `<remoteid>` | no |  |  | Pull the object's active version source from a remote system (Version Management). |
| `--tr` `<request>` | no |  |  | Pull all objects bound to a transport request (mutually exclusive with object name and --package). |
| `--user` `<sap-user>` | no |  |  | Filter --tr lookups by transport task owner (case-insensitive). Only valid with --tr. |

### Examples

- Pull a single class

  ```bash
  abap pull ZCL_MY_CLASS --type CLAS
  ```
- Pull a whole package

  ```bash
  abap pull --package ZPKG --limit 50
  ```
- Pull all objects bound to a transport

  ```bash
  abap pull --tr DEVK900001
  ```
- Pull textpool files alongside the source

  ```bash
  abap pull ZCL_MY_CLASS --textpool
  ```

## `abap run`

Execute an ABAP class (classrun) or a static method via the bundled runner wrapper; returns stdout + exit code (read-only). The wrapper route (--method) requires a system whose ADT classrun endpoint injects method arguments; otherwise it returns WRAPPER_INPUT_UNAVAILABLE.

```bash
abap run [options] <class-name>
```

### Arguments

| Argument | Required | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `class-name` | yes |  | Target ABAP class name (e.g. ZCL_MY_THING). Local classes with `~` are rejected with LOCAL_CLASS_NOT_RUNNABLE. |

### Options

| Option | Required | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--method` | no |  |  | PUBLIC STATIC method name to invoke via ZCL_ABAP_VIBE_RUNNER. When omitted, the class is run via ADT classrun (if_oo_adt_classrun~main). NOT available on systems whose ADT classrun endpoint does not inject method arguments: the call then fails with WRAPPER_INPUT_UNAVAILABLE — use the direct classrun path (`abap run <class>`) instead. |
| `--args` | no | `"{}"` |  | JSON object of method arguments, mapped to IMPORTING parameters (case-insensitive). Must be a JSON object, not array/null. |
| `--timeout` | no | `30000` |  | Maximum execution time in ms. Wrapper path enforces server-side via cl_abap_runtime; classrun path uses ADT endpoint timeout (~5min) plus CLI-side AbortController fallback. |
| `--dry-run` | no | `false` |  | Plan only — print the request envelope without invoking ADT classrun. |
| `--json` | no | `false` |  | Emit the unified JSON envelope on stdout; --pretty-json indents. |

### Examples

- Trigger classrun (no --method)

  ```bash
  abap run ZCL_MY_THING
  ```
- Invoke a static method with arguments

  ```bash
  abap run ZCL_MY_HELPER --method compute --args '{"x":3,"y":5}'
  ```
- Dry-run with timeout

  ```bash
  abap run ZCL_LONG_RUN --timeout 60000 --dry-run
  ```
- Agent integration: JSON envelope

  ```bash
  abap run ZCL_FOO --method bar --args '{}' --json
  ```

## `abap select`

Query table data read-only via the bundled ICF /data endpoint (SE16N equivalent): --table ZTAB [--fields ...] [--where ...] [--limit N] [--offset N] [--order-by ...] [--count-only]

```bash
abap select --table <name> [options]
```

### Options

| Option | Required | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--table` `<name>` | yes |  |  | Target ABAP table or view name (e.g. ZTAB_FIXTURE). Uppercased and validated against DDIC on SAP side. |
| `--fields` `<csv>` | no |  |  | Comma-separated field names to project. Omit for all fields (large-object fields STRG/RSTR/LCHR/LRAW excluded, listed in data.excludedFields). |
| `--where` `<clause>` | no |  |  | Filter clause: FIELD OP VALUE joined by AND. Ops: = <> > >= < <= LIKE. Strings in single quotes ('' for escape), numbers bare, dates 'YYYYMMDD'. MANDT filter rejected (implicit session client). |
| `--limit` `<n>` | no | `100` |  | Maximum rows returned. SAP fetches limit+1 to detect truncation (data.truncated). |
| `--offset` `<n>` | no | `0` |  | Row offset for pagination. Deterministic pagination requires --order-by. |
| `--order-by` `<csv>` | no |  |  | Comma-separated FIELD:ASC\|DESC pairs, e.g. "ID:ASC,AMOUNT:DESC". |
| `--group-by` `<field>` | no |  |  | Aggregate: return one row per distinct value of <field> plus CNT (COUNT(*)), ordered by CNT descending. Mutually exclusive with --fields / --order-by / --offset / --count-only. |
| `--count-only` | no | `false` |  | Return only the matching row count (data.count); rows/fields omitted. |
| `--dry-run` | no | `false` |  | Plan only — print the query envelope without invoking the ICF endpoint. |
| `--json` | no | `false` |  | Emit the unified JSON envelope on stdout; --pretty-json indents. |

### Examples

- Basic query with filter and limit

  ```bash
  abap select --table ZTAB_FIXTURE --where "STATUS = 'X'" --limit 50
  ```
- Projection + sort + pagination

  ```bash
  abap select --table ZTAB_FIXTURE --fields "ID,AMOUNT" --order-by "ID:ASC" --limit 20 --offset 40
  ```
- Count matching rows

  ```bash
  abap select --table ZTAB_FIXTURE --where "AMOUNT > 100" --count-only
  ```
- Agent integration: JSON envelope

  ```bash
  abap select --table ZTAB_FIXTURE --where "STATUS = 'X'" --limit 50 --json
  ```
- Dry-run: zero SAP calls

  ```bash
  abap select --table ZTAB_FIXTURE --where "STATUS = 'X'" --dry-run
  ```

## `abap fields`

List the DDIC fields of a table or view (read-only). Two modes: `abap fields <table>` enumerates the fields of one object; `abap fields --find <f1>,<f2>...` returns every table that contains those fields (reverse lookup).

```bash
abap fields <table> [--json] | abap fields --find <f1>,<f2>,...
```

### Arguments

| Argument | Required | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `table` | no |  | Table or view name (e.g. VRSD). Uppercased. Required unless --find is given. |

### Options

| Option | Required | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--find` `<field1,field2,...>` | no |  |  | Reverse lookup: list every table that contains the given fields. Comma-separated. Mutually exclusive with the positional table name. |
| `--any` | no |  |  | With --find, return tables containing ANY of the requested fields (default: ALL). |
| `--with-text` | no |  |  | With --find, include DDIC short text (DD03T/DD04T) for each matched field. |
| `--as4local` `<A|I>` | no |  |  | With --find, the DDIC active/inactive version to scan. Default 'A' (active). Pass 'I' to include inactive / changed versions. |
| `--tabclass` `<class>` | no |  |  | With --find, restrict to a DDIC table class (TRANSP, VIEW, INTTAB, ...). |
| `--limit` `<n>` | no |  |  | Max matches to return (default 200, hard cap 5000). |
| `--json` | no |  |  | Emit a single JSON envelope (global flag). |

### Examples

- Field inventory as JSON

  ```bash
  abap fields VRSD --json
  ```
- Human-readable listing

  ```bash
  abap fields VRSD
  ```
- Reverse lookup: tables that record a change user + date

  ```bash
  abap fields --find CHANGED_BY,CHANGED_ON --tabclass TRANSP
  ```
- Reverse lookup: tables with a UNAM field

  ```bash
  abap fields --find UNAM
  ```

## `abap run-report`

Execute an activated REPORT and return its list output (read-only, via the bundled ICF /run/report endpoint). The report runs with DEFAULT selection values; only classic list output is captured. --format (raw\|tsv\|csv) and --param NAME=VALUE pass-through are supported.

```bash
abap run-report <report> [--variant <name>] [--format raw|tsv|csv] [--param NAME=VALUE]...
```

### Arguments

| Argument | Required | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `report` | yes |  | Executable program name (TRDIR subc = 1), e.g. ZR_MY_REPORT. |

### Options

| Option | Required | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--variant` `<name>` | no |  |  | Selection variant to apply instead of the plain default values. |
| `--format` `<raw|tsv|csv>` | no |  |  | Output format. 'raw' (default) keeps SAP's list layout (with `\|` and `-----` separator bars). 'tsv' / 'csv' extract the columns to a tabular form. The transformation is client-side; the 'output' field always carries the raw SAP list so callers can switch formats without re-running the report. |
| `--param` `<NAME=VALUE>` | no |  |  | Ad-hoc selection-screen parameter, repeated. Forwarded to the SAP-side handler which echoes the list of params back in `data.params`. Apply them by changing report defaults or creating a variant. |

### Examples

- Run a report and print its list

  ```bash
  abap run-report ZR_MY_REPORT
  ```
- Run with a selection variant, as JSON

  ```bash
  abap run-report ZR_MY_REPORT --variant VAR1 --json
  ```
- Run with --format tsv for machine-readable rows

  ```bash
  abap run-report ZR_MY_REPORT --format tsv
  ```
- Pass selection-screen params (forwarded to SAP, echoed in response)

  ```bash
  abap run-report ZR_MY_REPORT --param P_USERNAME=DEVELOPER --param P_MAX=10
  ```

## `abap list`

List ABAP objects in a package (read-only, ADT quickSearch-backed). Useful for cleaning up scratch objects or auditing a package before mass pull/push.

```bash
abap list --package <pkg> [--type <type>] [--limit <n>]
```

### Options

| Option | Required | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--package` `<package>` | yes |  |  | Filter by package (e.g., $TMP). Required. |
| `--type` `<type>` | no |  |  | Filter by object type (CLAS, PROG, INTF, ...). |
| `--limit` `<n>` | no |  |  | Max results (default 20). |

### Examples

- List everything in $TMP

  ```bash
  abap list --package '$TMP'
  ```
- List every local scratch class

  ```bash
  abap list --package '$TMP' --type CLAS
  ```
- Limit the result set

  ```bash
  abap list --package '$TMP' --type CLAS --limit 50
  ```

## `abap delete`

Delete an ABAP object from SAP (lock → delete → unlock). Type is required to avoid ambiguity; --yes is required for non-interactive confirmation; a transport request is required for non-$TMP objects (matching `abap push` semantics).

```bash
abap delete <object> --type <type> [--tr <request>] --yes
```

### Arguments

| Argument | Required | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `object` | yes |  | Object name (e.g., ZCL_MY_CLASS, ZR_USER_CHANGES). |

### Options

| Option | Required | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--type` `<type>` | yes |  |  | Object type code (CLAS, PROG, INTF, FUGR, TABL, ...). |
| `--tr` `<request>` | no |  |  | Transport request number (required for non-$TMP packages). |
| `--yes` | yes |  |  | Confirm the deletion. Required — there is no implicit confirmation. |

### Examples

- Delete a local $TMP class

  ```bash
  abap delete ZCL_ZR_CHK9 --type CLAS --yes
  ```
- Delete a transport-bound object

  ```bash
  abap delete ZR_OLD --type PROG --tr NDK900123 --yes
  ```

## `abap push`

Push local ABAP files to SAP: lock → set source → syntax check → activate → unlock.

```bash
abap push [options] [files...]
```

### Arguments

| Argument | Required | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `files` | no |  | Files to push (positional, variadic). |

### Options

| Option | Required | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--all` | no |  |  | Push all .abap files under the scan root (sourceDir or current dir; honours .abapignore). |
| `--tr` `<transport>` | no |  |  | Transport number override for unbound objects. |
| `--check-only` | no |  |  | Syntax check only; do not activate. Not supported for ICF-routed or channel-routed JSON files (DDIC / HTTP / TRAN / XSLT / TTYP / MSAG / DDLS) — those are validated during push. |
| `--no-activate` | no |  |  | Lock + write + skip check + skip activate + unlock. |
| `--dry-run` | no |  |  | Plan only — no mutating ADT calls. |
| `--fail-fast` | no |  |  | Stop at the first failing file (default: --keep-going). |
| `--atomic` | no |  |  | Validate all files first; write nothing if any file fails validation. |
| `--yes` | no |  |  | Confirm in non-interactive mode. |

### Examples

- Push a single file

  ```bash
  abap push src/zcl_demo.clas.abap --tr DEVK900001
  ```
- Push all files under cwd

  ```bash
  abap push --all --tr DEVK900001 --yes
  ```
- Syntax check only (no activation)

  ```bash
  abap push src/zcl_demo.clas.abap --check-only
  ```

## `abap check`

Validate ABAP source code (syntax / content / atc).

```bash
abap check [syntax|content|atc] [options]
```

### Options

| Option | Required | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--variant` `<variant>` | no |  |  | ATC check variant (required with `check atc`). |
| `--all` | no |  |  | Check all .abap files under the scan root (sourceDir or current dir). |
| `--changed` | no |  |  | Check only files changed since the SAP version. |
| `--strict` | no |  |  | Treat warnings as failures. |
| `--out` `[file]` | no |  |  | Persist raw ATC worklist to a file (only with `check atc`); defaults to .abap/atc/<variant>-<timestamp>.json. |
| `--files` `<files...>` | no |  |  | Shortcut: run syntax mode on the given files (equivalent to `abap check syntax <files...>`). |

### Examples

- Syntax check

  ```bash
  abap check syntax src/zcl_demo.clas.abap
  ```
- Local-only validation

  ```bash
  abap check content src/zcl_demo.clas.abap
  ```
- ATC check with persisted worklist

  ```bash
  abap check atc src/zcl_demo.clas.abap --variant Z_ATC_VAR --out
  ```

## `abap test`

Run ABAP Unit tests for an object and report the summary plus failing tests (read-only).

```bash
abap test [options] <object>
```

### Arguments

| Argument | Required | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `object` | yes |  | ABAP object to test — a class or program name (e.g. ZCL_MY_THING). Resolved through the ADT object repository. |

### Options

| Option | Required | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--type` `<tadir>` | no |  |  | Object type filter for name resolution (CLAS, PROG, …); needed only when the name matches several object kinds. |
| `--risk` `<levels>` | no | `"harmless"` | harmless, dangerous, critical | Comma-separated risk levels to execute (default: harmless). |
| `--duration` `<levels>` | no | `"short"` | short, medium, long | Comma-separated duration levels to execute (default: short). |
| `--all` | no | `false` |  | Run every risk level and every duration level (instead of the defaults). |
| `--strict` | no | `false` |  | Treat warning alerts as failures. |

### Examples

- Run the default (harmless / short) ABAP Unit tests

  ```bash
  abap test ZCL_MY_THING
  ```
- Run every risk and duration level

  ```bash
  abap test ZCL_MY_THING --all
  ```
- Treat warnings as failures

  ```bash
  abap test ZCL_MY_THING --strict --json
  ```
- Agent integration: read summary + failures from the envelope

  ```bash
  abap test ZCL_MY_THING --json
  ```

## `abap search`

Search for ABAP objects in SAP system

```bash
abap search [options] <query>
```

### Arguments

| Argument | Required | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `query` | yes |  | Search query (supports * wildcard) |

### Options

| Option | Required | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--type` `<type>` | no |  |  | Filter by SAP ADT object type. Common values: CLAS, INTF, PROG, FUGR, TABL, TABL/DT (transparent table), TABL/DB (pooled), TABL/DY (append structure), DOMA, DTEL, STRU, MSAG, TYPE, TTYP. |
| `--limit` `<n>` | no | `20` |  | Maximum results per page |
| `--page` `<n>` | no | `1` |  | Page number (1-based) |
| `--exact` | no |  |  | Exact name match (mutually exclusive with --fuzzy) |
| `--fuzzy` | no |  |  | Substring match (default) |
| `--package` `<package>` | no |  |  | Filter by package |
| `--page-all` | no |  |  | Fetch all results in one request (cap = --page-all-max × --limit; mutually exclusive with --page) |
| `--page-all-max` `<n>` | no | `50` |  | Page-count cap that sizes the --page-all single request |

### Examples

- Filter by type

  ```bash
  abap search ZCL_* --type CLAS --limit 50
  ```
- Exact name match

  ```bash
  abap search ZCL_DEMO --exact
  ```
- Fetch all results in one request

  ```bash
  abap search ZCL_* --page-all
  ```

## `abap create`

Create a new ABAP source object (CLAS, INTF, PROG, FUGR) and activate it

```bash
abap create <type> <name> [options]
```

### Arguments

| Argument | Required | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | yes | CLAS, INTF, PROG, FUGR, DEVC, TABL, STRU, DOMA, DTEL, ENQU, VIEW, SHLP, NROB, HTTP, TRAN, XSLT, TTYP, MSAG, DDLS, SRVB, SRVD, BDEF, DCLS, DDLX, DDLA | Object type |
| `name` | yes |  | Object name |

### Options

| Option | Required | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--package` `<package>` | yes |  |  | Target SAP package (required) |
| `--description` `<desc>` | yes |  |  | Object description (required) |
| `--tr` `<transport>` | no |  |  | Transport number |
| `--no-activate` | no |  |  | Create the object but do not activate it |
| `--template` `<template>` | no |  |  | Skeleton template |
| `--no-pull` | no |  |  | Skip the create-then-pull local copy (default: pull after create) |
| `--check-only` | no |  |  | Validate the proposed object without creating it |
| `--audit` | no |  |  | Include the before-checksum (extra SAP round-trip, off by default) |
| `--overwrite` | no |  |  | When pulling the new object back, replace an existing local file (default: keep the local draft) |
| `--file` `<path>` | no |  |  | abap-file-format JSON input (required for TABL/STRU/DOMA/DTEL/ENQU/VIEW/SHLP/NROB/HTTP/TRAN/XSLT/TTYP/MSAG/DDLS/SRVD/DCLS/DDLX/DDLA) |
| `--func` `<name>` | no |  |  | With FUGR: create a function module (FUGR/FF) inside the existing function group <name> |
| `--software-component` `<swcomp>` | no |  |  | With DEVC: software component of the new package (default: inherited from the super package) |
| `--transport-layer` `<layer>` | no |  |  | With DEVC: transport layer of the new package (default: inherited from the super package) |
| `--package-type` `<type>` | no |  | development, main, structure | With DEVC: package type |
| `--yes` | no | `false` |  | Confirm in non-interactive environments. |
| `--non-interactive` | no | `false` |  | Alias of --yes. |

## `abap status`

Show local vs SAP sync status as a standardised changedParts list.

```bash
abap status [options]
```

### Options

| Option | Required | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--remote-only` | no |  |  | Only remote-only differences. |
| `--local-only` | no |  |  | Only local-only differences. |
| `--limit` `<n>` | no | `20` |  | Bounds the result; truncated: true when capped. |
| `--since` `<iso-date>` | no |  |  | Only files modified at or after the date (YYYY-MM-DD[THH:mm:ss]). |
| `--all` | no |  |  | Include unchanged entries. |

### Examples

- Default sync status

  ```bash
  abap status
  ```
- Only remote-only

  ```bash
  abap status --remote-only --limit 50
  ```

## `abap transport`

Manage SAP transport requests (list / create / show / resolve / assign).

```bash
abap transport <list|create|show|resolve|assign> [options]
```

### Options



### Examples

- List transports

  ```bash
  abap transport list
  ```

## `abap deploy`

Deploy bundled ICF ABAP service to SAP.

```bash
abap deploy [options] | abap deploy status [options]
```

### Options

| Option | Required | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--tr` `<transport>` | no |  |  | Transport number (required when --package is not $TMP). |
| `--package` `<package>` | no | `"$TMP"` |  | Target SAP package (default $TMP — local, no transport needed). |
| `--dry-run` | no |  |  | Plan only — make no mutating SAP calls. |
| `--diff` | no |  |  | Report per-file source differences. |
| `--dev` | no |  |  | Deploy the global-class development form (maintainers; skips the release merge). |
| `--force` | no |  |  | Bypass safety guards (forced: true in the result). |
| `--yes` | no |  |  | Confirm in non-interactive mode. |

### Examples

- Deploy to $TMP (no transport)

  ```bash
  abap deploy --yes
  ```
- Deploy the global-class development form (maintainers)

  ```bash
  abap deploy --dev --yes
  ```
- Deploy to a custom package

  ```bash
  abap deploy --package ZPKG --tr DEVK900001 --yes
  ```
- Read-only status probe

  ```bash
  abap deploy status
  ```

## `abap profile`

Manage global connection profiles (list / show / add / set / test / delete / export / import).

```bash
abap profile <command> [options]
```

### Options

| Option | Required | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--url` `<url>` | no |  |  | SAP system URL. |
| `--client` `<client>` | no |  |  | SAP client number. |
| `--username` `<user>` | no |  |  | SAP username. |
| `--language` `<lang>` | no |  |  | SAP language. |
| `--password` `<password>` | no |  |  | Password (stores credential in keychain). |
| `--remove-password` | no |  |  | Drop the stored password from keychain. |
| `--insecure` | no |  |  | Skip SSL certificate verification (development only). |
| `--ca` `<path>` | no |  |  | PEM CA certificate to import into ~/.abap-cli/certificates/ and bind to this profile. |
| `--clear-ca` | no |  |  | Remove the CA certificate setting. |
| `--file` `<path>` | no |  |  | Bundle file path for export / import. |
| `--with-passwords` | no |  |  | Include passwords in the export bundle (warned opt-in). |
| `--overwrite` | no |  |  | Update profiles that already exist on import. |
| `--yes` | no |  |  | Confirm in non-interactive mode. |

### Examples

- Add a profile

  ```bash
  abap profile add DEV --url https://... --username DEV --password ***
  ```
- Test a profile

  ```bash
  abap profile test DEV
  ```
- Export profiles

  ```bash
  abap profile export --file profiles.json
  ```

## `abap inspect`

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

### Options

| Option | Required | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--structure` | no |  |  | Include structure elements. |
| `--includes` | no |  |  | Include class include parts. |
| `--locks` | no |  |  | Include lock / transport ownership (read-only). |
| `--package` | no |  |  | Include the object package name. |
| `--activation` | no |  |  | Verify active vs latest source per part (read-only; detect stale activation). |

## `abap diff`

Compare local files against SAP (read-only) with a per-part change summary.

```bash
abap diff [options] [file]
```

### Arguments

| Argument | Required | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `file` | no |  | Single file to diff (mutually exclusive with --all/--remote/--local-only). |

### Options

| Option | Required | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--all` | no |  |  | Compare the whole workspace. |
| `--remote` | no |  |  | Only remote-only differences. |
| `--local-only` | no |  |  | Only local-only differences. |
| `--limit` `<n>` | no | `20` |  | Bounds the result. |

- Diff a single file

  ```bash

  ```


## `abap dumps`

List recent ST22 ABAP runtime dumps through the read-only ADT feed.

```bash
abap dumps [options]
```

### Options

| Option | Required | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--limit <n>` `<n>` | no | `20` |  | Maximum number of recent dump summaries to return. The limit is sent to ADT as $top. |
| `--user <name>` `<name>` | no | `"current SAP login user"` |  | Filter to an SAP user. Omit to use the current SAP login user; pass an empty value to query all users. |

### Examples

- List the most recent runtime dump summaries

  ```bash
  abap dumps
  ```
- Agent integration: restrict the result to five compact entries

  ```bash
  abap dumps --limit 5 --json
  ```
- Query all users (override default login-user filter)

  ```bash
  abap dumps --user ""
  ```

## `abap types`

Print the canonical CLI type ↔ TADIR PGMID/OBJECT ↔ DDIC tabclass mapping. Pure local — no SAP call. Surfaces the non-obvious mappings that cost real time when joining CLI write paths to TADIR queries (CLI HTTP ↔ TADIR SICF, CLI STRU ↔ TADIR TABL + DD02L-TABCLASS=INTTAB, etc.).

```bash
abap types [--json] | abap types <type> [--json]
```

### Arguments

| Argument | Required | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | no |  | Optional CLI type code to look up (e.g., STRU, HTTP, PROG). |

### Options

| Option | Required | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--tadir-object` | no |  |  | With a single type, print only the TADIR OBJECT value (one line, no table). |
| `--json` | no |  |  | Emit a single JSON envelope (global flag). |

### Examples

- Print the full type catalog

  ```bash
  abap types
  ```
- Look up a single type

  ```bash
  abap types HTTP
  ```
- Print only the TADIR object for STRU (for use in scripts)

  ```bash
  abap types STRU --tadir-object
  ```

## `abap report-stuck`

Record a stuck-agent report locally (feedback loop)

```bash
report-stuck --goal <text> --tried <text> --where <cmd>
```

### Options

| Option | Required | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--goal` `<text>` | yes |  |  | What the agent was trying to do |
| `--tried` `<text>` | yes |  |  | What the agent already tried |
| `--where` `<cmd>` | yes |  |  | Which command it was stuck on |

### Examples

- Record a stuck push attempt.

  ```bash
  abap report-stuck --goal "push zcl_demo" --tried "retried 3x" --where "abap push"
  ```


### Options



### Examples

- Create a MIME folder under $TMP

  ```bash
  abap mime create /zntf_ui --package '$TMP' --yes
  ```


## `abap validate:aff`

Validate JSON files against official abap-file-format (AFF) canonical schemas (Draft 2020-12).

```bash
abap validate:aff <file-or-dir> [--wire <wire-dir>]
```

### Arguments

| Argument | Required | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `file-or-dir` | yes |  | A JSON file or directory of JSON files to validate. |

### Options

| Option | Required | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--wire` `<wire-dir>` | no |  |  | Also recursively validate every JSON under a wire directory. |

### Examples

- Validate a single AFF file

  ```bash
  abap validate:aff src/zmy_basic.tabl.json
  ```
- Validate every AFF file under a directory

  ```bash
  abap validate:aff src/
  ```
- Validate a wire payload directory

  ```bash
  abap validate:aff src/zt_x.tabl.json --wire path/to/wire
  ```
